text:
Logan Mailloux missed the first month on injured reserve, and St. Louis sent Adam Jiricek and Theo Lindstein down to make room when he was activated on Nov. 10. Four games in, he has four points, including a goal and two assists in the 8-6 win over Anaheim.

The usage is the part to believe. He is playing 19 minutes a night, up from 16:46 last season, and he has been on the ice for 60% of the Blues' power-play chances after 7% a year ago. That role change is what earns him our breakout flag. The scoring pace (one point a game against 0.19 last season) is four games of noise, and our range for his points rate is far lower than what he is posting now.

The profile has a clear shape. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him getting to the home-plate area in front of the net at a 93rd-percentile rate last season, with 40% of his shots off the rush. Evolving-Hockey had him below replacement level, with his team creating little when he was out there. If he keeps the power-play time, he gets the chance to rewrite that.
